ev.section: OMNIQUANT: OMNIDIRECTIONALLY CALIBRATED QUANTIZATION FOR LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
ev.quote: # OMNIQUANT: OMNIDIRECTIONALLY CALIBRATED QUANTIZATION FOR LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
Codes are available at https://github.com/OpenGVLab/OmniQuant.

contribution.value: OmniQuant is a differentiable PTQ method for LLMs that learns weight clipping (LWC) and equivalent transformation (LET) parameters via block-wise error minimization, working for both weight-only and weight-activation quantization.

ev.quote: we introduce an Omnidirectionally calibrated Quantization (OmniQuant) technique for LLMs, which achieves good performance in diverse quantization settings while maintaining the computational efficiency of PTQ by efficiently optimizing various quantization parameters
We employ a calibration dataset consisting of 128 randomly selected 2048-token segments from WikiText2 (Merity et al., 2016)
we evaluate quantized models by reporting the perplexity of language generation experiments, specifically on Wiki-Text2 (Merity et al., 2016), PTB (Marcus et al., 1994))

key_results.value: LLaMA-13B at W2A16: OmniQuant PPL 13.21 vs GPTQ 5.5e3 (huge gap at 2-bit weight-only)

ev.quote: LLaMA-13B is quantized into W2A16, OmniQuant achieves a perplexity of 13.21, while GPTQ incurs a significant increase in perplexity to 3832

key_results.value: LLaMA-1-7B at W4A4: OmniQuant average zero-shot acc 52.65% vs SmoothQuant 38.41%, surpassing LLM-QAT (41.27%) by +6.22%

ev.quote: in the LLaMA-7B, OmniQuant even surpasses the recent QAT method, LLM-QAT (Liu et al., 2023b), by an impressive margin of +6.22%

key_results.value: W4A4 average accuracy gain across LLaMA models: +4.99% to +11.80% over best prior PTQ baseline

ev.quote: OmniQuant markedly enhances the average accuracy by +4.99% ~ +11.80% across various models at W4A4 quantization

key_results.value: LLaMA-7B W4A16g128 deployment via MLC-LLM: 134.2 tokens/s vs FP16 69.2 tokens/s (1.94x faster) and 3.8GB weight memory vs 12.6GB

value.hardware: NVIDIA A100-80G via MLC-LLM (LLaMA-7B W4A16g128: 134.2 vs 69.2 tokens/s)

ev.quote: models with W4A16g128 and W2A16g128 quantization almost double the inference speed

strengths.value: Achieves QAT-level accuracy with PTQ-level training cost: LLaMA-2-70B quantized in 16h on a single A100-40G with only 128 samples.

ev.quote: the LLaMA-2 model family size 7-70B can be processed with OmniQuant on a single A100-40G GPU within 1-16 hours using 128 samples

strengths.value: Versatile across configurations: handles W4A4, W6A6, W4A16, W3A16, W2A16 for both weight-only and weight-activation quantization.

ev.quote: Extensive experiments validate OmniQuant's superior performance across diverse quantization configurations such as W4A4 (4-bit weight, 4-bit activation), W6A6, W4A16, W3A16, and W2A16

strengths.value: Adds zero deployment overhead: learnable clipping and equivalent transform fuse into quantized weights, leaving inference graph unchanged.

ev.quote: OmniQuant introduces no extra computation or parameters for the quantized model because the clipping threshold in LWC and equivalent factors in LET can be fused into quantized weights

strengths.value: Generalizes to instruction-tuned LLaMA-2-chat with strong win rate vs RTN and parity or better than AWQ at W3A16g128.

ev.quote: In LLaMA-2-7b-chat, OmniQuant matches AWQ with a 50% win rate but surpasses RTN more (80.3% vs. 69.4%)

weaknesses.value: Training time is roughly 5x slower than GPTQ, even though it stays much faster than QAT methods.

ev.quote: our proposed method necessitates a training time that is approximately 5× greater than GPTQ, it remains markedly faster than QAT methods

weaknesses.value: MLC-LLM kernel support for INT3/INT2 inference is suboptimal, limiting actual speedup of low-bit configs.

ev.quote: MLC-LLM's support for INT3/INT2 is currently suboptimal, particularly for INT3

weaknesses.value: Real-device deployment is shown only for weight-only quantization, since W4A4 and W6A6 lack hardware support.

ev.quote: we only explore the deployment of weight-only quantization in this study due to that W4A4 and W6A6 quantization methods lack out-of-the-box hardware support

weaknesses.value: Learnable equivalent transformation gives only slight gain on LLaMA weight-only, indicating it is not always essential.

ev.quote: For weight-only quantization, LET significantly boosts OPT's performance but offers a slight enhancement for LLaMA

limitations.value: Tested only on data-center GPUs (A100-40G, A100-80G); no experiments on edge devices such as Jetson, mobile, or laptop GPUs.

ev.quote: speed in NVIDIA A100-80G

limitations.value: Does not evaluate safety, refusal, bias, jailbreak or toxicity behaviour after quantization.
Reports only mean perplexity and accuracy with no error bars, multiple seeds, or significance tests.
Energy consumption and per-token latency are not reported, only aggregate throughput in tokens/s.
